entities.name: Query protein 143 aa
observations: Exact sequence match to UniProt P78567, fungal histone H2B from Agaricus bisporus; identity and coverage are 100%, E-value 5.18e-81.
Length is 143 aa; calculated molecular weight is 15,165.2 Da; theoretical pI is 10.16; estimated charge at pH 7 is +16.67.
The N-terminal region is lysine/arginine-rich and low complexity, consistent with a flexible histone tail; the central region is compatible with a compact histone fold.

Pfam detects Histone PF00125.31 at residues 38-117 with i-Evalue 4.6e-21; CBFD_NFYB_HMF PF00808.30 overlaps at residues 58-114 but the exact H2B match supports interpreting the sequence as histone H2B rather than NF-YB.
Sequence-derived estimates do not account for post-translational modifications, processing, or oligomerization.

source_tools.relevance: All sequence properties, domain calls, and exact-match evidence

entities.name: Histone H2B
observations: Curated fungal H2B annotations describe a core nucleosome component involved in DNA packaging and chromatin regulation.
H2B forms H2A-H2B heterodimers within the histone octamer; the octamer contains two copies each of H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 and wraps approximately 147 bp of DNA.
Annotated functions include DNA binding, structural constituent of chromatin, and protein heterodimerization; localization is nucleus and chromosome.
Histone H2B N-terminal tails can carry regulatory post-translational modifications, but specific modifications cannot be established from this sequence alone.
